title: Multi-scale radiative-transfer model of the protoplanetary disc DoAr 44
question: Construct a comprehensive global multi-scale kinematic equilibrium radiative-transfer model for the pre-transitional disc of DoAr 44, spanning from the accretion region to the outer disc.

what.value: SED measurements from XMM-Newton, ASAS-SN, SkyMapper, Gaia, APASS, SDSS, Pan-STARRS, 2MASS, WISE, Spitzer/IRAC, Spitzer/MIPS, IRAS, AKARI, Herschel/PACS, Herschel/SPIRE, JCMT, and ATCA via VizieR

evidence.quote: The measurements of the SED were taken from the following surveys, publications and catalogues, using mostly Vizier (cite: ochsenbein2000vizier):
- ATCA, $\SI{3}{\milli\meter}$ (cite: ricci2010dust).

evidence.quote: The stellar parameters were set according to previously published works (cite: andrews2009protoplanetary; bouvier2020probing), $r_\star = 2.0\,R_\odot$, $T_\star = 4750\,{\rm K}$, $M_\star = 1.4\,M_\odot$.

recipe.goal: Construct mean Halpha spectrum and reduce VLTI visibilities
recipe.method: Piece-wise linear interpolation of 15 archival VLT Halpha spectra onto 200 equidistant points between 654.5 and 658.0 nm to compute a point-wise mean and standard deviation; reduce VLTI/GRAVITY data using Gravity Pipeline in EsoReflex.
assumptions: Mean Halpha profile corresponds approximately to an axially-symmetric mean state of the system

recipe.goal: Fit simple analytic visibility models to VLTI and ALMA data
recipe.method: Fit a homogeneous ellipse + point source + halo model to VLTI/GRAVITY visibilities, and a narrow elliptical delta-ring + halo model to ALMA Band 7 visibilities using MCMC, then rescale VLTI and ALMA visibilities into unit-less quantities.
key_parameters: Initial MCMC: 32 walkers, 10^4 steps; second iteration: 64 walkers, 10^5 steps, 30% burn-in; omega < 180 deg
assumptions: Uninformative prior; infinitely thin elliptical ring (delta-ring) for outer disc; homogeneous ellipse for inner disc

recipe.goal: Model the accretion region and innermost disc with radiative transfer
recipe.method: Use Pyshellspec/Shellspec with a central STAR (interpolated PHOENIX spectrum), a spherical SHELL of hot gas, and an innermost DISC to fit VLT Halpha spectra and VLTI/GRAVITY visibilities, and derive the mass accretion rate.
key_parameters: Fixed inner disc inclination i = 40 deg and position angle = 147 deg; stellar parameters r_* = 2.0 R_sun, T_* = 4750 K, M_* = 1.4 M_sun
assumptions: LTE (Saha equation for electron density), single-scattering radiative transfer, constant shell temperature, spherical shell geometry

recipe.goal: Model the outer disc and intermediate disc with radiative transfer and derive dust mass
recipe.method: Scan parameters of outer DISC (40-60 au) to fit ALMA Band 7 visibilities and SED, add warm intermediate DISC (0.2-1 au) to fit mid-IR SED deficit, and integrate vertical and radial density profiles to obtain outer disc dust mass.
key_parameters: Outer disc 40 to 60 au (8600 to 12900 R_sun), dust grain size a = 1 um, 90% water ice + 10% forsterite, intermediate disc 43 to 215 R_sun (0.2 to 1 au)
assumptions: Power-law density and temperature profiles, vertically isothermal disc, solar metallicity Z = 0.0122, dust composition of 90% water ice and 10% forsterite

score_reason: All raw observational data (ALMA, VLT, VLTI, VizieR SED) and the core modelling codes (Shellspec/Pyshellspec, emcee) are public, and best-fit model parameters are tabulated. However, the ALMA visibility extraction/averaging steps, exact SED flux table, assumed source distance, and trial-and-error parameter scan grids are not fully specified.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA and ESO/VLTI datasets are publicly available in archives, and the analytic MCMC visibility fitting (step 2) as well as the parametric radiative transfer fits produce concrete numerical values for disc inclinations, ring radii, and accretion rates.
